title: AI is reshaping the power investment landscape
gist: Wood Mackenzie expects AI data centres to drive a power-sector investment supercycle across gas, renewables, storage, grids and manufacturing, while warning that announced pipelines are inflated and outcomes have widened. US signed large-load capacity stands at 195 GW. APAC data centre consumption is forecast to more than triple to 980 TWh by 2030, mostly in China. Cost allocation through large-load tariffs and China's dominance of battery supply chains are key swing factors.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie expects a supercycle of infrastructure investment across renewables, gas-fired generation, storage, transmission and new technologies, driven by AI data centres, but says the range of possible outcomes has widened.
insights.speaker: Allen Wang
insights.so_what: Investors face broad power-capex upside, but project selection and policy risk matter more than ever.
